To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) patients with PD have difficulty comprehending sentences that are complex syntactically, (2) this difficulty is exacerbated when patients must perform a secondary task, (3) patients who have difficulty comprehending complex sentences at baseline have difficulty comprehending even the simplest sentences when they are performing a secondary task, and (4) the difficulty in comprehending sentences is not evident in patients' response times.

(1) PD patients with impaired baseline sentence comprehension were sensitive to resource demands of secondary task, (2) PD patients without impaired baseline sentence comprehension showed no effect of secondary task, and (3) control subjects showed an effect of secondary task.

patients with Parkinson's disease (1) show difficulty in understanding sentences when their cognitive resources are limited, (2) have difficulty understanding sentences with complex center-embedded clauses regardless of the secondary task condition, and (3) show a greater sensitivity to secondary task resource demand when they are already impaired in understanding sentences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processes underlying sentence comprehension in Parkinson's Disease (PD).
the cognitive processes underlying sentence comprehension in patients with idiopathic Parkinsons disease (PD) and in healthy controls.
the role of cognitive resource limitations in sentence comprehension in patients with Parkinson's disease (Parkinson's Disease).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the comprehension of the most difficult sentences is impaired in PD patients with a baseline impairment in sentence comprehension.
PD patients' sentence processing difficulty is related to limited cognitive resources.
cognitive resource limitations contribute to sentence comprehension deficits in PD, although other factors may also be involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the comprehension of sentences in PD patients is not only impaired in the presence of cognitive demands, but the comprehension impairment is more severe in the presence of more demanding cognitive resources.

the sentence comprehension difficulties observed in PD are not due to deficits in the perceptual processing of the sentence, the semantic processing of individual lexical items or the integration of semantic information, but instead are due to limited cognitive resources that may be shared by sentence comprehension and other cognitive functions.

the sentence comprehension deficit in Parkinson's disease is not simply a matter of slowed processing, but also a matter of reduced capacity to allocate resources to the task of sentence comprehension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive resource hypothesis can account for the sentence comprehension difficulties observed in PD patients.

the sentence comprehension deficit in PD patients with impaired baseline sentence comprehension may be due to a deficit in processing the information that is not due to the difficulty of the sentence itself, but rather to the difficulty in processing the information in the sentence.
cognitive resource limitations contribute to sentence comprehension deficits in Parkinson’s disease.
